author: richard
text: No, gender is a grammatical classification. While it is a cultural assignment, it is as old as human language, is consistent between languages as far as I know (I've only studied four), and does not change. Gender in the way you are using it, the way it has come to be misused globally in rapid fashion, was first put forth by the psychiatrists, Robert Stoller and Ralph Greenson, at a conference of psychoanalysts in 1963. Stoller and Greenson were practitioners of Freud's pseudoscience. To the extent Stoller and Greenson (fellow Afro-Asiatics of Freud) meant gender to refer to a degree of masculinity or femininity in one's behavior, regardless of sex, I have no objection. To the extent they meant gender to refer to a gradation of the sex binary (a common tactic of the psychoanalyst; e.g., LGBT can be simplified to H, they are all homosexuals; similarly, infantophiles, pedophiles, pedohebephiles, hebephiles, and ephebephiles are all pedophiles, defined as those sexually attracted to minors), it's just another neo-Marxist pseudoscience.
